content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED ruling and states its grounds, so the rule governing permissible grounds for UNDERDETERMINED applies to it.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse.", "room": "'never a ground' and 'decides nothing by itself' -- strict reading: the both-readings character of a single verse may not be cited as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED at all, and the judge's lead stated reason does exactly that; lenient reading: the mention of ambiguity is mere description and the operative ground is the mutual answering of each side's supports, which would be clean -- I weighed the judge's own ordering, which places the both-readings admission first as the stated reason for the ruling.", "why": "The judge rested its UNDERDETERMINED ruling on the fact that Matthew 1:16 admits both readings, which the rule expressly forbids as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED."}
